title: W09-[Feature] Resolve Stellar collateral by verified asset identity in the creation form
body:
Two Stellar assets can share a code. Creators and reviewers need the exact collateral identity in the proposal before on-chain publication is implemented.

**Scope**  

Use [SEP-11](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0011.md) identity for classic assets and derive the Stellar Asset Contract address with the SDK for the Testnet passphrase. Pin that C-address in the draft collateral field. Display the asset code and issuer, or XLM for native. Use `CreateMarketModal.jsx`, `frontend/src/lib/backend.mjs` and the review summary.

Seed fixtures with native XLM and two seven-decimal synthetic `REVTEST` assets using distinct deterministic test issuer public keys. Show synthetic entries only in explicit fixture mode. In the normal Testnet UI, show XLM and any explicitly configured, verified allowlist entries. Exclude mainnet asset IDs, real issuer listings, swaps and on-chain admission from this issue.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Assets sharing a code display distinct issuer identities and save the selected verified contract address.
- A removed or unavailable entry is labeled and cannot be silently replaced. Existing legacy draft values stay readable.
- The creator and reviewer see the same pinned asset in the stored revision. The UI identifies fixture assets as Testnet.

**PR evidence**  
Include duplicate-code, wrong-network and legacy `native` fixtures, screenshots and `npm test`, `npm run build`, and `npm run check:icons` results.

Follow the [contributor guide](https://github.com/Altacon-Labs/RevMarket/blob/327f3cb/CONTRIBUTING.md). For funded work, apply through Drips and wait for official assignment. Include the issue link in the PR.

title: W08-[Feature] Implement deterministic AMM quotes for binary outcome shares in Rust
body:
The JavaScript AMM fixture describes expected behavior. A reviewed Rust quote module will let the future market contract and tests share one integer pricing model.

**Scope**  
Implement pure buy and sell quotes in a shared `contracts/amm-math` crate. Use the binary fixed-product formulas in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, with [Gnosis FPMM](https://github.com/gnosis/conditional-tokens-market-makers/blob/master/contracts/FixedProductMarketMaker.sol) as a model reference. RevMarket uses its documented conservative fee rounding.

Use checked `i128` math in seven-decimal base units. Require input and pre/post reserves in `1..=10^18` base units. Accept fee rates `0..=1,000 bps` and use 30 bps as a test fixture. Buy fee is `ceil(gross input × bps / 10,000)`. Round the remaining bought-side reserve up. For sells, find the maximum whole complete sets that preserve the reserve product and positive reserves. Sell fee is `ceil(gross collateral released × bps / 10,000)`. Reject zero net input or output. Return output, fee and both next reserves. Swap reserve roles for **NO**.

**Acceptance criteria**

- With reserves 100/100 and zero fee, a 10-unit YES buy returns 19 shares and leaves reserves 91/110. Selling those 19 shares against 91/110 returns 9 collateral and leaves 101/101. A 10-unit sell payout would decrease the reserve product. Cover the mirrored **NO** path and fee rounding.
- Zero or unusable reserves, invalid input, bounds and arithmetic failure return defined errors.
- Include numeric boundaries and quote invariants with deterministic repeatable inputs. Document units and rounding.

**PR evidence**  
Include formulas, vectors and native Rust test results. The cap and fee range are RevMarket Testnet design parameters. Keep transfers, LP shares, storage and trading UI out of this issue.

Follow the [contributor guide](https://github.com/Altacon-Labs/RevMarket/blob/327f3cb/CONTRIBUTING.md). For funded work, apply through Drips and wait for official assignment. Include the issue link in the PR.

title: W07-[Feature] Add a Soroban factory registry for approved market implementations
body:
The repository models a factory in JavaScript tests, but the Rust workspace currently contains only the market contract. Start with an on-chain registry that future deployment can query.

**Scope**  
Add `contracts/factory` to the existing Cargo workspace. The ABI is `__constructor(operator: Address)`, `approve_version(version: u32, wasm_hash: BytesN<32>)`, and `get_version(version: u32) -> Option<BytesN<32>>`. Use Soroban's [address authorization](https://stellar.org/blog/developers/auth-entication-and-authorization-in-blockchain) for operator approval. Version 0 and all-zero hashes are invalid. Store an append-only version-to-hash mapping with an explicit storage lifetime policy. Emit a version approval event containing version and hash.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The operator can register and query a version. Unknown versions return None. Repeated registration fails, even with the same hash.
- Real Soroban authorization tests cover permitted registration and rejection without the administrator's authorization.
- The new crate builds to WASM and existing legacy tests still pass.

**PR evidence**  
Document the public methods, event and storage lifetime. Include `npm run test:contracts` and `npm run build:contracts` results. Child deployment, proof of WASM availability, reviewer authorization, collateral admission and trading are separate scopes.

Follow the [contributor guide](https://github.com/Altacon-Labs/RevMarket/blob/327f3cb/CONTRIBUTING.md). For funded work, apply through Drips and wait for official assignment. Include the issue link in the PR.
